--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[RT-1] Unbounded high-frequency broadcast
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L220)
Evidence: The client publishes position and animation every 100ms (two data channels) via localParticipant.publishData with DataPacket_Kind.LOSSY and no interest/area-of-interest filtering. This produces ~20 messages/sec per client going into LiveKit.  
Impact: Fan-out multiplies by recipients (producers × subscribers) causing O(N^2) message volume per room; LiveKit/network/CPU will be overloaded and messages dropped as concurrent users grow.  
Fix: Reduce publish frequency and batch channels, add interest management (spatial partitioning / selective subscriptions) or server-side aggregation to limit per-producer fan-out.

--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[RT-2] No sequence/timestamp or replay on data packets
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L220) and src/controller/RemotePlayersController.tsx (L1-L160)
Evidence: Data payloads are plain JSON with no sequence number or timestamp and are sent LOSSY; RemotePlayersController trusts most-recent values and requires both channels before rendering.  
Impact: Packet loss, reordering, or reconnects produce stale, missing, or inconsistent world state (invisible or jumping players) with no way to reconcile missed updates at scale.  
Fix: Add monotonic sequence numbers and timestamps to packets, accept partial updates, and implement snapshot/replay or authoritative reconciliation on reconnect.

finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[RT-1] Unbounded high-frequency broadcast
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L220)
Evidence: The client publishes position and animation every 100ms (two data channels) via localParticipant.publishData with DataPacket_Kind.LOSSY and no interest/area-of-interest filtering. This produces ~20 messages/sec per client going into LiveKit.  
Impact: Fan-out multiplies by recipients (producers × subscribers) causing O(N^2) message volume per room; LiveKit/network/CPU will be overloaded and messages dropped as concurrent users grow.  
Fix: Reduce publish frequency and batch channels, add interest management (spatial partitioning / selective subscriptions) or server-side aggregation to limit per-producer fan-out.

--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[RT-2] No sequence/timestamp or replay on data packets
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L220) and src/controller/RemotePlayersController.tsx (L1-L160)
Evidence: Data payloads are plain JSON with no sequence number or timestamp and are sent LOSSY; RemotePlayersController trusts most-recent values and requires both channels before rendering.  
Impact: Packet loss, reordering, or reconnects produce stale, missing, or inconsistent world state (invisible or jumping players) with no way to reconcile missed updates at scale.  
Fix: Add monotonic sequence numbers and timestamps to packets, accept partial updates, and implement snapshot/replay or authoritative reconciliation on reconnect.

--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[RT-3] No backpressure buffering / silent drops on slow publishes
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L220)
Evidence: publishData is awaited inside send locks (positionSendLock/animationSendLock) that prevent concurrent sends; if publishData blocks/slow, subsequent sends are skipped silently until the lock clears.  
Impact: Under LiveKit slowness or network latency, clients will silently drop updates (lost frames), creating large gaps in state and hard-to-debug data loss during bursts or partial outages.  
Fix: Implement a bounded send queue with drop policy (drop-oldest or coalesce), expose backpressure metrics, and adaptively throttle sends or disconnect persistently slow clients.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[RT-4] Silent LiveKit fallback hides outages
File: src/lib/livekit.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: Module-level init attempts to connect to LiveKit and exposes a roomServiceFallback that returns empty/mock data when LiveKit is unreachable, without surfacing failure states to callers.  
Impact: If LiveKit control plane fails, tokens/endpoints may still appear functional while clients cannot join, causing mass connection failures and poor operational visibility.  
Fix: Surface health status from the module, fail token/room endpoints explicitly when LiveKit is down, and add alerting/health-check endpoints.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[RT-5] Rendering requires both channels before showing player
File: src/controller/RemotePlayersController.tsx (L1-L160)
Evidence: RemotePlayersController filters participants to those with both networkAnimations and networkPositions before including them in remote players.  
Impact: Loss/delay of one channel (animation or position) causes players to be omitted, producing visible dropouts at scale even when partial updates exist.  
Fix: Allow partial updates with decay logic (render with most-recent available data) and use timestamps to expire stale values.

--- INFO ---

[RT-6] LiveKit used as transport; no in-app WS server
File: package.json and src/pages/api/universe/connection.ts
Evidence: Project uses livekit-client/server-sdk and issues LiveKit AccessTokens from Next API routes; there is no long-lived WebSocket server in the app itself.
